g.passage: Carmela was the name on my badge that winter, though the keepers at the lighthouse station outside Tbilisi mostly called me 'the voice.' I interpreted for Pavel, a Czech engineer hired to inspect the old signal lamp, which now guided nothing but the fishing boats that crossed the reservoir at night. On our first morning, the station chief explained the rule: visitors could not climb above the third landing without a keeper beside them, and the keepers never had time. I translated this briskly, as I had translated a hundred regulations, and Pavel nodded the way people nod at weather. By the fourth day, though, I had watched him wait on that landing for hours, his notebook open to blank pages, while the keepers drank tea below and shrugged. When the chief repeated the rule yet again, I heard my own voice go flat and careful, choosing each word as if it might break. I did not soften it this time. I let him hear exactly how little sense it made.

g.passage:
When you left the noodle stall on Hamra Street last Thursday, Karim, you were certain I had lied to the old cook. I understand why. He asked, in Arabic, whether I was your mother, and you heard me answer with something much longer than 'no.' You assumed I had claimed a title I have not earned. I was annoyed, I admit, that you would not let me explain on the walk home; I even rehearsed a little speech about trust and fairness. But I have since thought about your face at the counter, how quickly the steam hid it, and I am less interested in being right. What I actually said was 'I am the one who gets to feed him today.' My Arabic is clumsy, and perhaps it sounded like more. If it did, I am sorry. Come back to the stall with me on Sunday, and you can ask him yourself what he heard.

seed.topicSeed: a rented farmhouse in Galicia; a young apprentice and a master carpenter about keeping a family business open

g.passage: 'Nobody pays for dovetails anymore,' Alba said during my first week in the rented farmhouse in Galicia where she kept her carpentry shop. I was nineteen, and Ivan was the name she shouted whenever a clamp slipped, which was often. Her grandfather had founded the business; the lease, she admitted, ran out in spring, and the bank preferred customers who bought flat-pack furniture. Still, every morning she made me cut joints by hand until my palms blistered. __One evening I found her ledger open on the bench, with every column of the last year totaled in red.__ I said nothing about it. The next morning she handed me the chisel again, and I began to see that she was not training a worker for her shop. She was training someone to carry its craft somewhere else after the doors closed.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It suggests that Alba is hiding the shop's wealth from the narrator to avoid paying him more.
It provides evidence that undercuts Alba's hopes and reframes her insistence on training.
It shows that the narrator secretly plans to take over the shop's accounts from Alba.
It marks the moment when the narrator decides to quit his apprenticeship for good.
g.explanation: 앞에서 임대가 봄에 끝나고 은행이 조립식 가구를 선호한다는 위기가 제시된다. 밑줄 문장의 빨간 장부는 가게가 살아남기 어렵다는 증거를 보여 준다. 그 뒤 화자는 Alba의 고된 훈련이 가게를 위한 것이 아니라 가게가 문을 닫은 뒤에도 기술을 이어 갈 사람을 키우는 것임을 깨닫는다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 장부가 적자를 보여 주므로 반대이고, D는 화자가 다음 날도 끌을 받으므로 틀리다.

seed.relationship: a violin student and an exacting teacher
seed.conflict: while one of them quietly changes their mind
seed.topicSeed: a vineyard at harvest in Tbilisi; a violin student and an exacting teacher while one of them quietly changes their mind

g.passage: Grapes do not hurry. So said Vesna, the strictest violin teacher in the hills above Tbilisi, who held her lessons among the vines at harvest so that her pupils would learn patience from the fruit. Anushka, her newest student, wanted to play fast. Each afternoon she raced through her scales, and each afternoon Vesna made her begin again, slower, while the pickers' baskets filled around them. On the last day of harvest, Anushka played a folk tune the pickers sang, quickly and brightly, and the pickers clapped and danced between the rows. Vesna said nothing. __That evening, she set aside the slow études she had planned for the winter and wrote out three dances in her own hand.__ In the morning she gave them to Anushka and told her that some fruit is for wine and some is for eating straight from the vine.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It shows that Vesna has grown impatient with Anushka and plans to stop teaching her.
It reveals that Vesna intends to perform the dances herself at the pickers' celebration.
It indicates that Vesna has silently revised her view of how Anushka should be taught.
It explains that the slow études were too difficult for a student of Anushka's age.
g.explanation: Vesna는 처음에 '포도는 서두르지 않는다'며 Anushka에게 느리게 연습하도록 반복해서 요구한다. Anushka의 빠른 민요 연주에 일꾼들이 춤추는 것을 본 뒤 Vesna는 아무 말도 하지 않는다. 밑줄 문장에서 그녀가 느린 연습곡을 치우고 춤곡을 직접 적는 것은 말없이 교육 방침을 바꾸었음을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이며, A와 D는 근거가 없고 B는 춤곡을 Anushka에게 준다는 내용과 어긋난다.

seed.relationship: a returning soldier and his younger sister
seed.conflict: over a witness account that differs
seed.openingStyle: 구체적인 사물이나 동작으로 시작(관사 The 로 시작하지 말 것)
seed.topicSeed: a metro platform in Galway; a returning soldier and his younger sister over a witness account that differs

g.passage: Coins rattled in the ticket machine as Maeve fed it, one at a time, refusing my help. My sister had been home from her deployment for nine days, and the metro platform in Galway was the farthest she had gone alone. On the radio that morning, a man who had served in her unit described the night their convoy was struck: smoke, shouting, a corporal carried out by Maeve herself. At breakfast, Maeve had told it differently. No one carried anyone, she said; the corporal walked, and she only held the door. I have wondered which of them is lying. But watching her now, counting the coins twice and pressing each one in as though it might be refused, I think the question is the wrong one. Perhaps she remembers holding the door because that is the part she can bear to have done.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Maeve?
options: She is openly skeptical of Maeve's account and resents her for contradicting the radio.
She is amused by Maeve's stubbornness and treats her return home as a minor event.
She is fearful of Maeve's changed temper and avoids speaking to her about the war.
She is tenderly perceptive, moving from doubt toward compassion for Maeve's memory.
g.explanation: 화자 Brigid는 처음에 라디오 증언과 언니의 말 중 누가 거짓말을 하는지 궁금해한다. 그러나 동전을 두 번 세며 조심스럽게 넣는 Maeve를 지켜보며 그 질문 자체가 잘못되었다고 생각한다. 마지막 문장에서는 Maeve가 견딜 수 있는 부분만 기억하는 것일 수 있다고 이해하려 한다. 따라서 의심에서 연민으로 나아가는 섬세한 태도인 D가 정답이며, A는 처음의 의심만 보고 원망까지 덧붙인 오답이다.

seed.relationship: a father and his stubborn son
seed.conflict: after a storm reveals what was buried
seed.topicSeed: an apartment stairwell in Manchester; a father and his stubborn son after a storm reveals what was buried

g.passage: After the storm, the stairwell of the old block on Wilmslow Road in Manchester smelled of wet plaster, and a section of wall beside the third landing had slumped away to reveal a small tin box wedged between the bricks. Tunde found it first. He was a man who announced everything, his cholesterol, the council's failings, the proper way to fold a shirt, and yet he slipped the box into his coat without a word. Dana, his son, who had not visited in a year and had come only because the power was out, watched him do it and said nothing either. They were alike in that, though neither would have admitted it; they had argued about who was more stubborn for most of Dana's life. Later, in the flat, Tunde opened the box at the kitchen table: a child's tooth, a hospital bracelet, a photograph of a boy on these same stairs. He pushed it across to Dana as though returning something borrowed.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Tunde and Dana?
options: Wry yet affectionate, noting their shared stubbornness and their hidden tenderness.
Harshly critical, blaming both men for allowing the old building to fall into disrepair.
Coolly detached, recording their actions without suggesting any feeling between them.
Openly sentimental, praising Tunde as a model father whom Dana has unfairly neglected.
g.explanation: 서술자는 Tunde가 콜레스테롤부터 셔츠 개는 법까지 모든 것을 떠벌린다고 가볍게 비꼬고, 두 사람이 누가 더 고집이 센지 평생 다퉜다고 말한다. 동시에 아들의 어린 시절 물건이 든 상자를 조용히 건네는 장면으로 숨겨진 애정을 드러낸다. 따라서 재치 있으면서도 다정한 시선인 A가 정답이다. C는 감정이 전혀 없다고 했지만 마지막 장면과 맞지 않고, D는 서술자가 한쪽 편을 들지 않으므로 틀리다.

seed.relationship: old rivals in a chess club
seed.conflict: about a debt neither will mention
seed.topicSeed: a lighthouse station in Nairobi; old rivals in a chess club about a debt neither will mention

g.passage:
Nairobi sleeps below the old beacon tower
where no ship has ever needed light,
and still the lamp turns, and still we come,
Baraka and I, to the chess club in its base.
He plays the Sicilian, as he has for thirty years.
I play badly, as I have for thirty years,
and neither of us speaks of the winter
he paid my rent and asked for nothing back.
Some debts are coins. Some are a chair
pulled out for you every Thursday,
a kettle already warm, a clock pressed
gently on your side when you are losing.
I have tried to repay it. He will not take it.
So I lose to him slowly, with great care,
and he pretends each time to be surprised.
g.question: Which choice best describes the speaker's attitude toward Baraka?
options: Resentful, because Baraka keeps reminding the speaker of the money he is still owed.
Grateful and fond, expressing an unspoken obligation through their ritual of play.
Competitive and bitter, determined at last to defeat Baraka after years of losing.
Indifferent, treating the weekly chess games as a habit with no deeper meaning.
g.explanation: 화자는 Baraka가 겨울에 집세를 내 주고 아무것도 요구하지 않았다고 말하며, 둘 다 그 일을 입에 올리지 않는다고 밝힌다. 또 의자를 빼 주고 주전자를 데워 두는 등의 작은 친절도 빚으로 여기며 갚으려 했지만 거절당했다고 한다. 그래서 정성껏 천천히 져 주는 체스 의식으로 고마움을 표현한다. 따라서 B가 정답이며, A는 두 사람 모두 빚을 언급하지 않는다는 내용과 반대이다.

seed.relationship: a sister and her younger brother's tutor
seed.conflict: over a map, a route or a way home
seed.topicSeed: a quiet library in Vienna; a sister and her younger brother's tutor over a map, a route or a way home

g.passage: On the first Tuesday of every month, I collected my younger brother Wolfram from the reading room of a quiet library near the Ringstrasse in Vienna, where his tutor, Anselm, taught him geography from maps older than our grandparents. I disliked Anselm at first. He was late, he hummed, and he insisted that Wolfram learn to walk home by landmarks rather than by the tram map I had drawn for him. I thought it was vanity, an old man's romance with the city. Then one winter evening the trams stopped in a snowstorm. I found Wolfram already halfway home, steering by the green dome of a church, the bakery with the brass pretzel, the fountain with the missing nose. He had not needed my map at all. I still think Anselm hums too much. But I no longer think his lessons were for show, and I have started, a little grudgingly, to notice landmarks myself.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Anselm?
options: Unchanged dislike, since the storm confirmed that his methods put Wolfram in danger.
Uncritical admiration, as she now regards him as the finest teacher in Vienna.
Reluctant respect, as she comes to value his methods despite lingering annoyance.
Amused indifference, as she treats his lessons as harmless but ultimately pointless.
g.explanation: 필자는 처음에 Anselm이 늦고 콧노래를 부르며 허영심으로 랜드마크 학습을 고집한다고 싫어했다. 그러나 눈보라로 트램이 멈춘 날 Wolfram이 랜드마크만으로 집에 오는 모습을 보고 그의 방법이 옳았음을 인정한다. 그럼에도 여전히 콧노래가 지나치다고 말하며 '조금 마지못해' 랜드마크를 보기 시작했다고 한다. 따라서 남은 불만 속의 마지못한 존중인 C가 정답이며, B는 비판이 남아 있다는 점을 놓쳤다.

seed.relationship: a ranger and a lost hiker
seed.conflict: about borrowed money and borrowed time
seed.topicSeed: a crowded wedding hall in Hamburg; a ranger and a lost hiker about borrowed money and borrowed time

g.passage: Three things I owed Katharina when I saw her again at my cousin's wedding in Hamburg: forty euros, a wool hat, and the two days of my life she had given back to me on a ridge in the Harz, when I was lost and stubborn and too proud to call for help. She was a park ranger then, impatient and sunburned, and she had lent me the money for the bus home without asking my name. Now she was a guest at the next table, laughing too loudly at a toast. I had rehearsed a gracious speech. Instead I pushed through the crowded hall holding a fifty-euro note and stammered something about interest. She looked at the money, then at me, and asked whether I still hiked alone. I admitted that I did. She folded the note back into my hand. 'Then you'll need the bus fare,' she said, and I was too grateful, and too embarrassed, to argue.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Katharina?
options: Resentful, because Katharina humiliates the narrator by refusing her money in public.
Nostalgic, longing to return to the ranger's life that Katharina once described.
Suspicious, since the narrator doubts that Katharina truly remembers the rescue.
Indebted and admiring, yet self-conscious about how to repay Katharina's kindness.
g.explanation: 필자는 처음부터 Katharina에게 진 빚을 돈, 모자, 되찾은 이틀이라는 목록으로 나열하며 큰 은혜를 느낀다. 준비한 연설 대신 말을 더듬으며 돈을 내미는 장면은 어떻게 갚아야 할지 몰라 쑥스러워하는 모습을 보여 준다. 마지막에 너무 고맙고 너무 부끄러워 반박하지 못했다는 말이 이를 확인한다. 따라서 D가 정답이며, A는 부끄러움을 원망으로 잘못 읽은 오답이다.

seed.relationship: a ferryman's daughter and a passenger
seed.conflict: about the proper way to say goodbye
seed.topicSeed: a ferry terminal in Seville; a ferryman's daughter and a passenger about the proper way to say goodbye

g.passage:
Joaquin, I am writing from the bench outside my father's ticket booth at the ferry terminal in Seville, where you stood last Sunday and asked me, quite seriously, how people here say goodbye. I laughed at you then, and I am sorry, but you must understand that nobody had ever asked me before. You had a list from a guidebook: the kiss on each cheek, the handshake, the wave from the deck. You wanted to do it properly. I told you there was no proper way, which was unkind, because there is, and you found it without me. When the horn sounded, you did not kiss or wave. You simply stood at the rail until the ferry turned the bend, the last passenger still facing the dock. My father says only fishermen and homesick people do that. I hope you will write and tell me which you are.

Marisol
g.question: Which choice best describes Marisol's attitude toward Joaquin?
options: Gently amused yet touched, coming to admire his sincere farewell.
Mildly irritated, finding his guidebook questions tiresome and naive.
Deeply suspicious, doubting that he truly intended to leave Seville.
Formally polite, offering travel advice as part of her father's business.
g.explanation: Marisol은 Joaquin의 진지한 질문에 웃었다고 고백하며 그의 안내서 목록을 가볍게 묘사한다. 그러나 그가 배 난간에 서서 끝까지 부두를 바라본 모습을 '제대로 된 방식'을 스스로 찾은 것이라고 인정한다. 마지막에 그가 어떤 사람인지 편지로 알려 달라는 말에서 애정 어린 관심이 드러난다. 따라서 A가 정답이며, B는 처음의 웃음을 짜증으로 오해했고 C와 D는 근거가 없다.
